one_month_reasoning: Nov 3 for Eaton's Q3 report is an aggregator estimate that Eaton has not confirmed. EDGAR shows no new 8-K since Jul 31. Eaton reported Q3 on Oct 31 in 2023 and 2024, so I put roughly 25-30% odds on a print inside the window (supervisor finding, which I accept). Management said at Laguna on Sep 16 that it is tracking toward the high end of the Q3 guide, so an in-window print leans slightly positive but mostly adds variance. The other in-window events are two-sided: the FOMC on Oct 27-28 (Polymarket, Sep 26: 67% odds of another 25bp hike after the Sep 16 hike, with the 10-year at 5.24%), late-October hyperscaler capex commentary, and Q3 prints from VRT, GEV and Schneider. Net: about symmetric around ~$433. I use lognormal monthly vol of 0.115, slightly above 39%/3.5 = 0.111, for the chance of an earnings print in the window.

fair_value.method: Blend of forward P/E (NTM EPS at Sep 2027 of ~$16.8, pro-forma ex-Mobility on ~380M post-split-off shares, x 26x = $437, weight 0.6) and FCF yield (NTM FCF/share ~$16.0 at a 3.6% yield = $444, weight 0.4). This is the ETN share price itself. The Mobility/Dana deal is a split-off that retires tendered ETN shares, so no ~$13 distribution comes out of the price in the base case (round-1 error corrected).

bear.story: By mid-2027 the market prices 2028 AI capex growth slowing to single digits. Orders roll over from the +41% pace, rates stay above 5%, and the multiple compresses to ~18-19x on ~$15.5-16 pro-forma NTM EPS. This repeats the Jan-Apr 2025 (-38%) and Jul-Dec 2025 (-22%) drawdowns.

base.story: ~12-13% EPS growth, H2 2026 margin step-up delivered, the Mobility split-off closes in Q1 2027 (retiring ~8-10M shares, $1.1B to debt, ~3% EPS dilution, no price drop), and Boyd integrates. The multiple holds ~26-27x on ~$16.8 NTM EPS.

bull.story: Hyperscaler 2027 capex beats the ~$1.3T forecasts and 2028 guides stay strong. Price/cost turns into a tailwind and margins reach the 28% target early. Buybacks resume in 2027 and the multiple re-rates to ~33x on ~$17.8 EPS.

thesis_break_reason: About 26% below spot and near the Dec 2025 low / 52-week low of $312. At $320, ETN is ~19x pro-forma ex-Mobility NTM EPS of ~$16.8, which only fits falling earnings: data-center order cancellations, a negative Electrical Americas rolling-order print, a failed H2 margin step-up, or a recession (Kalshi ~24% for 2027). I keep $320 rather than the supervisor's $330 because, with the 10-year at 5.24% and Fed hikes priced, a pure de-rating to ~20x could reach ~$335 with no fundamental damage. A break should be confirmed with order data.

reasoning: Base rates: ETN's 12-month returns since 2011 have a median of +14% and a 5th-95th percentile of -15% to +69%, and are negative 32% of the time. That sample is biased up by a 15-year re-rating from ~12x to ~30x, so I do not anchor on its median. Two 22-38% drawdowns in 2025 support a fat left tail. Round-2 corrections: (1) The supervisor showed, and I confirmed in the Jul 31 Form 425, that the Mobility/Dana RMT is a split-off by exchange offer with a pro-rata distribution only as a clean-up if needed. My round-1 ~$13/share mechanical price drop was wrong. I now value per share on ~380M post-split-off shares. Net EPS dilution is ~3%, which leaves NTM EPS at ~$16.8, since share retirement offsets part of my round-1 $0.8 haircut. (2) Rates were verified (Fed funds upper bound 4.00% effective Sep 17, 10-year 5.24%), so I keep 26x. (3) I drop the exact Goldman capex numbers from an X summary and the Polymarket recession figure from a snippet, and rely on Kalshi and Fool instead. Fair value is ~$440, ~2% above spot. The distribution mixes 80% lognormal (median $452, sigma 0.30) with 20% bear regime (median $345, sigma 0.35), and puts 15% on a partial clean-up distribution (~$6 average drop). That gives a median of ~$431, a mean of ~$451 and P(>=spot) of 0.50. Round 1's median of ~$427 was biased down by the phantom distribution. I did not go further above 0.50 because rates, leverage and the 2028 capex cliff keep the left tail heavy. Research was limited to 2 SEC fetches this round.
